done_when: Every review and plan read records its model, effort, chat id and token use in Forge's run records, the same way worker rounds do

findings.body: Raise: Not done. Forge does not pass `--stream-engine-output` to Autoreview. [Autoreview's engine code](https://github.com/openclaw/agent-skills/raw/refs/heads/main/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview) adds `--json` to Codex only when that opt-in flag is set. On a normal Codex review, the launcher therefore receives no `thread.started` or `turn.completed` events for `_spent` to parse, and the run end lacks chat and token use. The `review_codex` proof misses this because its fake helper always invokes Codex with `--json`.
findings.title: Not done: Every review and plan read records its model, effort, chat id and token use in Forge's run records, the same way worker rounds do

findings.body: Raise: Scale. Autoreview can split a large review into multiple provider passes, but `_spent` replaces `found` at each new Codex thread and each Claude result. For a review split into two passes, the single Forge run end records only the final pass's chat and tokens, understating the review's cost. The named tests exercise only one pass.
findings.title: Chunked reviews record only the last pass's token use

why: Reviews and plan reads record no model, effort, chat or token use, so nobody can tell what they cost or whether a lighter setting would do
